authoring: Gameplay geometry (our layer). Rig tuning constants (F/MATS/GAIN/BIAS/LN) stay in the rig. Derived from the rig SHA above; a rig reshape re-opens this file.
extractor_contract: per section: rig export -> this sidecar -> absent section = hull does not support the feature (not an error).

_notes.note: The motor station — this is the seat STATIONS.helm_seat sits on, tiller in reach. Widest of the three (0.34 m fore-and-aft) because it is sat on under way, not just perched on.

DECK._notes_convention: Every thwart top sits SEAT - FLOOR = 0.240 m above the floor plane, so all three are step-overs, not walls. Per the 2026-07-22 ruling these become game-side colliders sourced from these notes — never holes in the DECK polygon.

_excluded.cleats: Superseded — CLEATS is now modeled (bow_1 stem ring bolt + stern_port quarter-knee ring). No deck/mid cleats: an open 5.2 m boat does not carry them.
_excluded.motor: The outboard is a separate layer (renderMotor, own 212x168 cell, pivot-aligned). This hull bakes the clamp pad + MOUNT / motorMount(dir,opts).
_excluded.oars: Oars are a separate overlay layer in the HULL cell — see ROWLOCKS for the hull-side fittings.

CLEATS.provenance: rig PAINTER / painter(dir,opts) — iron ring bolt through the breasthook at the stem head, station(0.962) sheer + 0.050 (exact).
CLEATS.note: Answers the open question in the previous pass: yes, she gets a mooring point, and the same one the dory got — painter rove through a ring in the breasthook, inboard end knotted there for good.
CLEATS._ruled: was _confirm: no modelled ring/cleat in the rig; M2-38 wants every hull moorable, so a bow painter tie-point is authored at the stem head. RULED: ACCEPTED AS AUTHORED (owner, 2026-07-22) — the data-only painter point stands, NO visible ring/fitting is added to the art ('option 1 is fine for now'); a visible fitting may be revisited later. ⚠ REOPENED BY ART, 2026-07-25 (small-craft rig kit v2): the rig now MODELS a visible iron ring bolt at this point, so the 'NO visible ring/fitting' half of the 2026-07-22 ruling no longer describes the art. The tie-point itself also moved: station(1.0) -> station(0.962), pos y 2.6 -> 2.4024 m, z 0.80 -> 0.79832 m. Recorded, not deleted — the owner re-rules.

CLEATS.provenance: rig STERN_EYE / sternEye(dir,opts) — through the port quarter knee, 0.028 above the knee plate (exact).
CLEATS.note: The alongside case: under power she comes to the wharf and needs bow AND stern lines. Offset to PORT to stay clear of the outboard clamp on the transom centreline; mirror x if the wharf convention lands starboard-to. No starboard twin, no transom cleat.

ROWLOCKS.provenance: rig OARLOCK_U=0.42 — socket plate + thole pin baked into the gunwale (exact); loom_seat = rig oarlockPt(side), the point the oar pivots about when pulling.
ROWLOCKS.note: A rower on the mid thwart (u 0.48) has these 0.31 m aft of the seat — hands meet amidships. Oars are a separate layer: renderOars(dir,{state,t}) + oarHandles(dir,opts).

STATIONS.provenance: rig ROW_SEAT / rowSeat(dir,opts) — mid thwart top centre, station(0.48) keel + SEAT (exact).
STATIONS.note: The rowing station. Occupied only when the oars are in the locks; the motor station takes over otherwise.

STATIONS.provenance: rig HELM / helmSeat(dir,opts) — stern bench top centre, station(0.15) keel + SEAT (exact).
STATIONS.note: Tiller in reach of the outboard clamp. pilotStand(dir,opts) puts the feet on the floor at y=-1.25, in the pocket immediately forward of it.

PAINT.model: slots -> derived ramps. The hull carries five paint slots (hull topsides, trim/sheer band, cove line, bottom, interior); each slot is ONE base hex and the rig derives its ramp (rampFrom) in OKLCH with a locked lightness curve, chroma capped at C_CAP=0.115, shadows rotated toward 258deg and highlights toward 92deg.
PAINT.defaults: bottom falls back to trim; interior falls back to bare wood (WOOD ramp). Oars ("oar") and outboard cowling ("cowl") keep fixed ramps and never follow the paint.
PAINT.canonical: harbour-white keeps the hand-tuned pass-1 arrays, so that scheme is bit-identical to the original bake.
PAINT.persistence: store a boat's colourway as the 4-5 base hexes, not as a baked sheet — render(dir,{paint:{...}}) at load, or export one PNG per scheme.
PAINT.picker: chipWall() returns the legal grid a UI should offer: 10 hue families x 6 value bands, chroma peaking midtone. A raw hex from code is accepted and clamped the same way.
